title: The Orbit of a Point
teaches: Definition of an orbit under iteration.
visual: A complex plane with a fixed point z=0 and a moving red dot representing z_0. The function f(z) = z^2 is displayed. The red dot jumps from z_0 to z_1, then z_2, tracing a path that spirals outward as its magnitude doubles each step.
narration: We begin by observing the orbit of a single point under iteration. Starting with an initial value z_0, we repeatedly apply the function f(z) = z^2 to generate a sequence: z_1 = f(z_0), z_2 = f(z_1), and so on.

title: The Unit Circle Boundary
teaches: Distinction between bounded and unbounded orbits based on initial magnitude.
visual: A unit circle is drawn in blue. Points inside the circle (|z| < 1) are colored green and their orbits shrink toward zero. Points outside (|z| > 1) are colored red and their orbits explode to infinity. Points exactly on the circle remain on the boundary.
narration: Notice how the magnitude of z determines its fate. If |z_0| < 1, the orbit converges to zero; if |z_0| > 1, it diverges to infinity. The unit circle acts as a critical boundary separating these two distinct behaviors.

title: Julia Sets for Quadratic Maps
teaches: Visualizing the Julia set as the boundary of chaotic behavior.
visual: The view zooms out to show a Mandelbrot-like fractal structure. The screen fills with a black region (the filled Julia set) and a white background. A thin, intricate, self-similar boundary separates them, highlighting points that neither converge nor diverge simply but exhibit chaotic sensitivity.
narration: For more complex functions, the boundary becomes fractal. This intricate curve is the Julia set, where points exhibit chaotic sensitivity to initial conditions. It represents the precise threshold between order and divergence.

title: Holomorphicity and Conformality
teaches: Why holomorphic functions preserve angles locally.
visual: A small grid of orthogonal lines is overlaid on the complex plane. As a point moves through the iteration f(z) = z^2 + c, the grid distorts but remains locally perpendicular (conformal). Labels appear showing 'Angle Preserved' at various points away from critical points.
narration: Finally, we recall that holomorphic functions are conformal, meaning they preserve angles locally. This property ensures that the geometric structure of small neighborhoods is rotated and scaled, but never sheared, during iteration.
